description: Approximately 100 km sample of low-relief Amazonis plains near 19 N, 203 E.

selection_diagnostics.initial_candidate: 16 N, 202 E: elevation -4545 to -3413 m, maximum grid-gradient slope 35.93 degrees; rejected for sharp terrain.
selection_diagnostics.final_reason: 19 N, 203 E has 178 m total relief across approximately 100 km and 95th percentile grid-gradient slope about 0.27 degrees; avoids the major sharp features in tested southern/western candidates.

processing: Validated PDS dimensions 11520 x 5632, MSB_INTEGER 16 bits, METER, record bytes 23040 and exact IMG size 129761280.
HDR agrees on binary layout but explicitly omits georeferencing; PDS bounds and half-pixel projection offsets define pixel-area edges 180..270 E and 0..44 N.
PDS IMAGE specifies direct metre topography with no scaling/offset keywords: identity conversion, not radius or counts.
Extracted integer window row=3092, col=2830, height=216, width=228; no DEM reprojection, resampling, smoothing, interpolation or upsampling.
Native equirectangular pixel dimensions retained; differing longitudinal ground spacing is explicitly recorded.
data_quality_notes: Native topography includes upstream interpolation where no MOLA shots exist; no per-cell observation mask was supplied.
Effective resolution unknown: 128 pixels per degree is grid spacing, not verified effective resolution.
No PDS missing-value constant or HDR ignore value is declared. All crop values retained, including valid zero; -32768 is an unused output sentinel, not an inferred source mask.
Crop selected from nearby candidates using actual topographic relief and gradient diagnostics. It is a regional smooth-plains sample, not crater-free ground at sub-grid scales.
Preview colour stretch uses 2nd-98th percentiles for visibility; it does not change DEM measurements. Display-only nearest-neighbour column selection corrects centre ground aspect ratio.
Terrain category describes regional volcanic-plains context, not mineralogical validation of every pixel.
citation: NASA/MGS MOLA Science Team, David E. Smith, GSFC; MEGDR v2.0, created 2003-03-21.
